newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold market moves in seasonal upturn.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold market moves in seasonal upturn.

text.p: Demand for gold in the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai is expected to step higher in November and December because of strong Bombay demand sparked by Indian festivals and economic reform, Dubai traders said on Sunday.

After a summer lull, Dubai souk traders said turnover in bullion and jewellery has taken off this month as Indian goldsmiths import stock in preparation for the Hindu festivals off Dassera and Diwali and India's second marriage season.
A decision by India's central bank to increase domestic liquidity as part of a reform programme to spur the country's economy has also been welcomed by the Dubai gold trade.

"With (India's) real estate market still depressed, the easing of pressure on liquidity as a result of latest RBI (Central Bank) initiative will help the Indian bullion market during the upcoming festivals and second leg of marriage season," Dubai-based Satco Global Trading said in a report.
Indian subcontinent demand is also expected to be aided by stable and sub-$400 an ounce bullion prices.
International spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $382.50-$383.00 an ounce, just above support at $382.00.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,285 UAE dirhams ($1,440.05), up from 5,254 dirhams on October 20.
Ten gram pieces were quoted at 453 dirhams, up from 449.
TT bars in the Bombay market was assessed at $1,690.
Summer demand from the Indian subcontinent for Dubai bullion was again subdued, partly reflected in Dubai import figures.
Dubai's import dipped to 26.5 tonnes in September, its lowest level since February, according to figures released by the World Gold Council (WGC) in the emirate.
"It was a tough season...sales went down during summer," one souk trader said.
The highest monthly import figure in the first nine months of this year was May at 33.2 tonnes, WGC figures show.
Total bullion imports since January have reached 254.599 tonnes, up from 244.883 tonnes the same period last year.

"While the demand for gold locally has also seen a rise, the traditional markets like India, Pakistan and Iran to which Dubai caters are also fuelling this rise," Rolf Schneebelli, WGC's Middle East and India head said in a statement.
Satco Global Trading quoted silver in Dubai at $160.11 a kg on Sunday, a 0.8 percent gain on the week. Silver in Bombay was assessed at $195.75 a kg.
Figures compiled by Dubai customs show silver re-exports from Dubai increased in September to a total of 63.4 tonnes, up from 53.2 tonnes in August.
India remained the biggest market for Dubai silver, importing 59.6 tonnes last month from 48.2 tonnes in August and 44.5 tonnes in September 1995.
Pakistani monthly demand held steady at two tonnes.
-- Steven Swindells, Dubai Newsroom, +971 4 6071255.
